title: Kinetics (reaction rate)
body: The kinetics of a chemical reaction is the rate at which an amount of reactants is converted to products per unit of time.
ced_evidence: 5.1.A.1 "the rate at which an amount of reactants is converted to products per unit of time"

title: Stoichiometry sets relative rates of change
body: The rates of change of reactant and product concentrations are determined by the stoichiometry in the balanced chemical equation.
ced_evidence: 5.1.A.2 "determined by the stoichiometry in the balanced chemical equation"

title: Factors that influence reaction rate
body: The CED names these factors as influencing the rate of a reaction.

items.label: Reactant concentrations
items.meaning: Influence the rate

items.label: Temperature
items.meaning: Influences the rate

items.label: Surface area
items.meaning: Influences the rate

items.label: Catalysts
items.meaning: Influence the rate

items.label: Other environmental factors
items.meaning: Influence the rate

ced_evidence: 5.1.A.3 "reactant concentrations, temperature, surface area, catalysts, and other environmental factors"

title: General rate law expression
body: \text{rate}=k[\mathrm{A}]^{m}[\mathrm{B}]^{n}
ced_evidence: 5.2.A.2 "the rate of a reaction as proportional to the concentration of each reactant raised to a power"

title: Order of reaction (individual and overall)
body: The power of each reactant's concentration in the rate law is the order with respect to that reactant, and the sum of those powers is the overall reaction order.
ced_evidence: 5.2.A.3 "The sum of the powers of the reactant concentrations in the rate law is the overall order"

title: Rate constant (k)
body: The proportionality constant in the rate law, whose value is temperature dependent and whose units reflect the overall reaction order.
ced_evidence: 5.2.A.4 "The value of this constant is temperature dependent and the units reflect the overall reaction order"

title: Find orders by comparing initial rates
body: Comparing initial rates of a reaction across experiments is the method to determine the order with respect to each reactant.
ced_evidence: 5.2.A.5 "Comparing initial rates of a reaction is a method to determine the order with respect to each reactant"

title: Zeroth-order integrated rate law
body: [\mathrm{A}]_t-[\mathrm{A}]_0=-kt
ced_evidence: 5.3.A.4 "Zeroth order: [A]t − [A]0 = −kt"

title: First-order integrated rate law
body: \ln[\mathrm{A}]_t-\ln[\mathrm{A}]_0=-kt
ced_evidence: 5.3.A.4 "First order: ln[A]t − ln[A]0 = −kt"

title: Second-order integrated rate law
body: \frac{1}{[\mathrm{A}]_t}-\frac{1}{[\mathrm{A}]_0}=kt
ced_evidence: 5.3.A.4 "Second order: 1/[A]t − 1/[A]0 = kt"

title: Linear plot that identifies reaction order
body: Order is identified by which concentration-versus-time plot is linear; the slope gives the rate constant.

items.label: Zeroth order
items.meaning: [A] vs. t is linear; slope = −k

items.label: First order
items.meaning: ln[A] vs. t is linear; slope = −k

items.label: Second order
items.meaning: 1/[A] vs. t is linear; slope = k

caution: Slope signs follow the integrated equations: negative for zeroth and first order, positive for second order. Name the plotted quantity (not just 'a line') when justifying the order.
ced_evidence: 5.3.A.2 "a plot of the natural log (ln) of the reactant concentration as a function of time will be linear"; 5.3.A.3; 5.3.A.4

expands_to.means: first order: plot ln[A] vs. t

hooks.when_to_use: To recall which quantity is plotted against time for orders 0, 1, 2.
hooks.caution: In the answer, state the order and the specific quantity that gives a straight line (e.g., ln[A] vs. time is linear, so first order), not just the phrase.

title: First-order half-life
caution: Half-life is constant (independent of concentration) only for first-order reactions.

title: Radioactive decay is first order
body: Radioactive decay processes provide an important illustration of first-order kinetics.
ced_evidence: 5.3.A.6 "Radioactive decay processes provide an important illustration of first order kinetics"

title: Elementary-step rate law from stoichiometry
body: The rate law of an elementary reaction can be written directly from the stoichiometry (coefficients) of the particles participating in the collision.
caution: This applies only to elementary steps, not to an overall reaction equation of a multistep mechanism.
ced_evidence: 5.4.A.1 "inferred from the stoichiometry of the particles participating in a collision"

title: Three-body elementary collisions are rare
body: Elementary reactions involving the simultaneous collision of three or more particles are rare.
ced_evidence: 5.4.A.2 "simultaneous collision of three or more particles are rare"

title: Requirements for a successful collision
body: Only a small fraction of collisions lead to reaction; a successful collision needs both of these.

items.label: Sufficient energy
items.meaning: Enough to overcome the activation energy requirements

items.label: Proper orientation
items.meaning: Orientation that allows bonds to rearrange in the required manner

ced_evidence: 5.5.A.2 "sufficient energy to overcome the activation energy requirements and orientations that allow the bonds to rearrange"

title: Maxwell-Boltzmann energy distribution
body: A distribution curve of particle energies used to qualitatively estimate the fraction of collisions with enough energy to react and how that fraction changes with temperature.

items.label: Horizontal axis
items.meaning: Particle (collision) energy

items.label: Vertical axis
items.meaning: Relative number (fraction) of particles at each energy

items.label: Activation energy marker
items.meaning: Energy threshold for reaction

items.label: Area beyond activation energy
items.meaning: Fraction of collisions with sufficient energy to react

items.label: Higher-temperature curve
items.meaning: Larger fraction of particles above the activation energy, so a faster rate

ced_evidence: 5.5.A.3 "Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution curve describes the distribution of particle energies"

title: Activation energy (forward)
body: The energy difference between the reactants and the transition state is the activation energy for the forward reaction.
ced_evidence: 5.6.A.3 "The energy difference between the reactants and the transition state is the activation energy for the forward reaction"

title: Reaction coordinate
body: The axis along which the complex set of motions involved in rearranging reactants to form products can be plotted.
ced_evidence: 5.6.A.2 "The reaction coordinate is the axis along which the complex set of motions..."

title: Single-step reaction energy profile
body: A plot of energy along the reaction coordinate from reactants, through a transition state, to products.

items.label: Vertical axis
items.meaning: Energy

items.label: Horizontal axis
items.meaning: Reaction coordinate

items.label: Reactants
items.meaning: Starting energy level

items.label: Transition state
items.meaning: Energy maximum between reactants and products

items.label: Products
items.meaning: Ending energy level

items.label: Activation energy
items.meaning: Energy difference from reactants to transition state (forward reaction)

items.label: Overall energy change
items.meaning: Energy difference between products and reactants

ced_evidence: 5.6.A.3 "from reactants, through a transition state, to products"; LO 5.6.A

title: Why elementary rate depends on temperature
body: The rate of an elementary reaction depends on temperature because the proportion of collisions energetic enough to reach the transition state varies with temperature.
caution: Arrhenius equation calculations are excluded from the AP Exam; use only the qualitative relationship between temperature, activation energy, and rate.
ced_evidence: 5.6.A.4 "proportion of particle collisions that are energetic enough to reach the transition state varies with temperature"

title: Reaction mechanism
body: A series of elementary reactions, or steps, that occur in sequence and whose components may include reactants, intermediates, products, and catalysts.
ced_evidence: 5.7.A.1 "a series of elementary reactions, or steps, that occur in sequence"

title: Mechanism steps must sum to the overall equation
body: The elementary steps, when combined, should align with the overall balanced equation of the reaction.
caution: The overall equation is only a validity check; identify catalysts, intermediates, and the rate-determining step by examining the individual steps.
ced_evidence: 5.7.A.2 "The elementary steps when combined should align with the overall balanced equation"

title: Reaction intermediate
body: A species produced by some elementary steps and consumed by others, so that it is present only while a reaction is occurring.
caution: Do not confuse with a catalyst: an intermediate is made then consumed, whereas a catalyst is consumed then regenerated.
ced_evidence: 5.7.A.3 "produced by some elementary steps and consumed by others"

title: Rate law from a mechanism with rate-limiting first step
body: If every elementary step is irreversible, or the first step is rate limiting, the rate law is set by the molecularity of the slowest (rate-limiting) elementary step.
ced_evidence: 5.8.A.1 "set by the molecularity of the slowest elementary step (i.e., the rate-limiting step)"

title: First step not rate limiting requires an approximation
body: If the first elementary reaction is not rate limiting, approximations such as pre-equilibrium must be made to determine the rate law expression.
ced_evidence: 5.9.A.1 "approximations (such as pre-equilibrium) must be made to determine a rate law expression"

title: Multistep reaction energy profile
body: An energy profile for a multistep mechanism built from the energetics of each elementary step.

items.label: Reaction coordinate axis
items.meaning: Horizontal axis spanning all steps

items.label: Transition state for each step
items.meaning: An energy maximum for each elementary step

items.label: Activation energy for each step
items.meaning: Barrier from that step's starting level to its transition state

items.label: Reaction intermediate(s)
items.meaning: Species between steps, at energies between transition states

items.label: Overall energy change
items.meaning: Energy of final products relative to initial reactants

ced_evidence: 5.10.A.1 "Knowledge of the energetics of each elementary reaction in a mechanism allows for the construction of an energy profile"

title: How a catalyst increases rate
body: A catalyst must increase the number of effective collisions and/or provide a reaction path with a lower activation energy relative to the original reaction coordinate.
caution: A complete answer cites the specific effect (more effective collisions or an alternate lower-Ea path), not just 'it speeds up the reaction'.
ced_evidence: 5.11.A.1 "increase the number of effective collisions and/or provide a reaction path with a lower activation energy"

title: Catalyst in a mechanism
body: A catalyst's net concentration is constant; it is frequently consumed in the rate-determining step and regenerated in a subsequent step.
caution: Cite the step evidence: the catalyst is consumed as a reactant in one step, regenerated as a product in a later step, and absent from the overall equation. Do not confuse it with an intermediate.
ced_evidence: 5.11.A.2 "the net concentration of the catalyst is constant"

title: Types of catalysis named in the CED
body: Catalysts that act through a new bound or covalent intermediate, each introducing new elementary reactions.

items.label: Binding to reactants (e.g., enzymes)
items.meaning: Reactants are oriented more favorably or react with lower activation energy; new intermediate has catalyst bound to reactant(s)

items.label: Acid-base catalysis
items.meaning: Covalent bonding in which a reactant or intermediate gains or loses a proton; introduces a new intermediate

items.label: Surface catalysis
items.meaning: A reactant or intermediate binds to, or forms a covalent bond with, the surface; introduces bound intermediate(s)
